title.rendered: Love the Lord Your God With All: The Gospel For Today

content.rendered:
Every Jewish home in first-century Israel recited the same prayer morning and evening. When a scribe asked Jesus which of all the commandments was the greatest, Jesus reached first for the words every listener had been praying since they could speak.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, September 20, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Jesus answered him, ‘The first of all the commandments is: “Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.” This is the first commandment.'”
Mark 12:29-30 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Every Jewish home in first-century Israel recited the same prayer morning and evening. Twice a day, from childhood to grave. “Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one.” The prayer was called the Shema, from the Hebrew word for “hear.” Every parent taught it to every child. Every synagogue opened with it. Every observant Jew would have known it by heart before they could read. When a scribe stopped Jesus in the Temple courts and asked which of all the commandments was the greatest, Jesus reached first for the words every listener had been praying since they could speak.

“The first of all the commandments is: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.” Jesus took the ancient Shema from Deuteronomy 6, added the fourth “with all” (mind, which the original had implied but not stated), and gave the scribe the Kingdom’s foundational commandment. Love God. Love Him totally. Love Him with everything you are.

The four dimensions Jesus names cover the whole of the human person. Heart, the seat of desire and affection. Soul, the deep animating life force. Mind, the intellectual and rational capacity. Strength, the physical body and its exertion. Every part of what makes you human is invited into the loving of God. The love commanded is not merely emotional. Not merely intellectual. Not merely religious. It is a whole-person orientation toward the One who made you.

The Passion Translation renders it: “Love the Lord your God with every passion of your heart, with all the energy of your being, with every thought that is within you, and with all your strength” (Mark 12:30 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And you shall love the Lord your God out of and with your whole heart and out of and with all your soul (your life) and out of and with all your mind (with your faculty of thought and your moral understanding) and out of and with all your strength” (Mark 12:30 AMPC). Out of and with. Every source of love in you flowing toward the One who created every source.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, the invitation of the Shema is still exactly what it was in the Temple courts that day. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, God is inviting you to love Him with the totality of who you are. Not just when you feel like it. Not just when you have time. Not just in church. With everything. With your desires. With your inner life. With your thinking. With your body. The commandment is total because the God who commands is worthy of total love. And here is the New Testament gospel underneath the Old Testament command. The ability to love Him this way is not something you generate through willpower. It is the natural response of a heart that has first been loved by Him in Christ. He loved us first. Our whole-person love flows back from the whole-person love He has already given.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You are worthy of the total love of my whole person. Every part of me was made for You. Today I offer You my heart, my desires, my affections. I offer You my soul, my inner life, the deep animating force of who I am. I offer You my mind, my thinking, my understanding. I offer You my strength, my body, my energy. Every source of love in me flows back to You, because You loved me first in Christ. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I love the Lord my God with all my heart, soul, mind, and strength. My whole person flows toward the One who made me. He loved me first. I love Him back with everything I am.
